s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with vomiting and abnormal cardiac findings
salient_findings: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 80s
Chest pain duration is 1 hour
Patient denies history of hypertension and diabetes
Temperature is 36°C
Heart rate is 79 beats per minute
Blood pressure is 92/56 mm Hg
Maximal cardiac impulse is in the right fifth interspace
Hepatic dullness is located in the left subcostal region
Initial serum troponin I level is 0.070 ng/mL
ECG shows negative P waves in lead I
ECG shows QRS complexes in leads V1 through V6 with activation of ventricle in right thorax
ECG shows diminishing QRS amplitude progression from V1 to V6
ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Coronary Angiography shows total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Transthoracic Echocardiogram shows right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle on the right side

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery and elevated serum troponin I level

shortlist.label: Right ventricular infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery and ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF

shortlist.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
shortlist.why_kept: Right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle on the right side on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, vomiting, and ECG changes including ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6, along with the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery on coronary angiography and the specific echocardiogram findings, strongly supports right ventricular infarction. The location of the maximal cardiac impulse in the right fifth interspace and the hepatic dullness in the left subcostal region also suggest an abnormal cardiac position, but the key diagnostic features point towards an infarction involving the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While the patient does have an acute myocardial infarction as indicated by elevated troponin and ECG changes, the specific involvement of the right ventricle and the unique echocardiogram findings make 'Right ventricular infarction' a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs inversus
rejected.why: The echocardiogram shows the right atrium and ventricle on the left and the left atrium and ventricle on the right, which could suggest dextrocardia, but the primary issue here is the infarction, not just the anatomical positioning.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There's no specific indication of cardiomyopathy in the provided information; the focus is on the acute event of infarction.

rejected.label: Coronary artery anomaly
rejected.why: The total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery is a significant finding, but it does not by itself indicate an anomaly; it's part of the infarction scenario.
